summary_en: This Phase 2 pilot study tests yttrium-90 radioembolization given with capecitabine and atezolizumab for colorectal cancer that has spread to the liver and cannot be surgically removed. Yttrium-90 is given to one or both liver halves (hemilivers), atezolizumab is given by IV every 3 weeks for 5 doses, and capecitabine is taken by mouth twice a day for 2 weeks, starting with each yttrium-90 treatment. The main outcome is not stated in the record; the study is Phase 2.
summary_es: Este estudio piloto de fase 2 evalúa la radioembolización con itrio-90 combinada con capecitabina y atezolizumab para el cáncer colorrectal que se ha extendido al hígado y no puede extirparse quirúrgicamente. El itrio-90 se administra en uno o ambos lóbulos hepáticos, el atezolizumab se da por vía intravenosa cada 3 semanas durante 5 dosis, y la capecitabina se toma por vía oral dos veces al día durante 2 semanas, comenzando con cada tratamiento de itrio-90. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el estudio es de fase 2.
who_for: Colorectal adenocarcinoma that cannot be surgically removed, with disease mainly in the liver.
Disease that progressed after two or more lines of systemic therapy.
Less than 50% of liver volume replaced by metastatic disease, per investigator.
Blood count, kidney, liver and clotting lab values within the stated limits.
not_for: Prior yttrium-90 therapy or prior external beam radiation to the liver.
Known mismatch repair deficiency, MSI-H, or high tumor mutational burden.
Prior treatment with CD137 agonists or anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-CTLA4 antibodies.
Active hepatitis B, active hepatitis C, HIV, or active tuberculosis.
History of autoimmune disease, apart from the listed exceptions.
